The video proceeds to show a dynamic range analysis of the image, indicating +4 Stops (+4 Stops) and -6 Stops (-6 Stops) which translates to a "TOTAL DYNAMIC RANGE of 10 STOPS". Subsequently, a man wearing a blue shirt and a grey beanie, headphones around his neck, speaks directly to the camera. He introduces concepts of contrast ratios and stops in photography and cinematography. He then highlights the difference between f-stops and t-stops; and how cinema often uses T-stops for light transmission. An image of the iris on a lens is then displayed. Following this a shot from the movie "The Hobbit" is displayed, and a light dynamic range map. The man then explains that when an item is said to be "a stop brighter, it means it's twice the brightness of the reference value referring to 18% gray". He then shows a chart of "STOP DIFFERENCE" and "CONTRAST RATIO" with "LIGHT DOUBLES THIS WAY" on the left and "LIGHT HALVES THIS WAY" on the right of the table. He explains the chart by indicating a "contrast ratio" from the range of stops 2 and 3. He concludes the video segment.
